column1: Okay, so let's say where we were. We have these rings associated to a discriminant, and I'm going to take the discriminants to be less than zero. So the uniform way of writing these rings is it's Z + Z(D + sqrt(D))/2, and this was a subring of the complex numbers. And when you describe the elements of this ring inside the complex numbers, they formed a lattice, and we started to look at the ideal theory of these rings.
column2: 好，我们回顾一下之前讲到哪里了。我们有与判别式相关联的这些环，这里我取判别式 D < 0。那么统一表示这些环的方式就是 Z + Z(D + √D)/2，它是复数域的一个子环。当你把这个环的元素放在复平面中描述时，它们构成一个格点（点阵），我们开始研究这些环的理想理论。

column1: So the first thing we observed was that if you had an ideal which was not equal to zero in this ring, then it had finite index. And we're going to need a name for that index pretty soon, so you could call that index |R_D/I|, but I'm going to call it the norm of I in general.
column2: 我们首先观察到的是：若该环中有一个非零理想 I，那么它在环中具有有限指数。我们很快需要给这个指数起个名字，你可以把该指数称为 |R_D/I|，但我通常称之为理想 I 的范数 N(I)。

column1: I'll say why in a second. The reason is that if you take a principal ideal, if I = alpha * R_D, then you find that the norm of I is the same as the norm of alpha. The index of this ideal we showed was that—remember the norm of the element, the norm of alpha is alpha * alpha-bar.
column2: 我马上解释为什么。原因是：如果你取一个主理想，若 I = alpha * R_D，你会发现 I 的范数就等于 alpha 的范数。我们之前证明过该理想的指数就是——记住元素的范数，也就是 alpha 的范数是 alpha * alphā。

column1: So for a general ideal, whether or not it's principal, it does still have a finite index, so we can associate to it an integer which is greater than or equal to 1, called the norm of the ideal.
column2: 因此对一般理想而言，无论是否为主理想，它仍然具有有限指数，所以我们能给它关联一个大于等于 1 的整数，称为该理想的范数。

column2: 好，现在如果你想进一步推进理想理论，我们想在某种程度上衡量 R_D 距离成为主理想整环（PID）有多远——距离主理想整环有多远。这需要严格精确化，但我们已经见过很多并非每个理想都是主理想的例子。然而，我们能否给出一个度量，来衡量它们偏离主理想的程度？

column1: So the idea in this was introduced in the mid-19th century, and first of all people generalized the notion of an ideal a bit. So how did they generalize the ideal? To what's called a fractional ideal. Peter, did you do fractional ideals last time? Okay, I'll do fractional ideals. But this is similar to what Peter gave to get to a notion of a group.
column2: 这个想法是在 19 世纪中叶被引入的，首先人们稍稍推广了理想的概念。他们是如何推广理想的呢？推广成了所谓的分式理想。彼得，你上次讲分式理想了吗？好，那我来讲分式理想。但这与彼得引入群概念的方式类似。

column1: A fractional ideal is a generalization of an ideal: it's an I which is a lattice in C stable under multiplication by R, and the only difference is it's not necessarily contained in R; it's contained in the quotient field of R, it's contained in Q(sqrt(D)), but not necessarily contained in the ring.
column2: 分式理想是理想的推广：它是一个理想 I，是 C 中的格点，在 R 的乘法下稳定，唯一的区别在于它不一定包含在 R 中；它包含在R 的分式域中，即包含在 Q(√D) 中，但不一定包含在环内。

column1: So I'll give you an example of a fractional ideal, perfectly reasonable example of a fractional ideal. It can't be the whole field because that wouldn't be a lattice; it has to still be this discrete subgroup under addition. So this is an ideal, it has to be a subgroup, so it's a discrete subgroup under addition, and you can multiply by elements in the ring and you stay in this. So an example of a fractional ideal that isn't an integral ideal is: you take an element beta which is in the field, which is nonzero but might not be in the ring, and then you consider the ideal I which is all multiples of R by beta, like you might take 1/2 of R, you multiply everything in R by 1/2.
column2: 我给你们举一个分式理想的例子，一个非常合理的例子。它不能是整个域，因为那就不再是格点了；它仍然必须是加法下的离散子群。所以这是理想，必须是子群，因此是加法下的离散子群，而且乘以环中元素后仍然落在其中。那么一个不是整环内部理想的分式理想的例子就是：你在域中取一个元素 beta，它非零，但可能不在环中，然后考虑由 beta 乘以 R 生成的理想 I，由 beta 的所有 R 倍数构成，比如你可以取 (1/2)R，把 R 中的每个元素都乘以 1/2。

column1: So for example, if R were the Gaussian integers—so here's the ring R of Gaussian integers, we might have the fractional ideal I, which is—sorry, this is Z[i]—we might have the ideal 1/2 * R, which would be the points here, and that's a lattice, it's just not contained in R, okay? So you can get slightly larger things than R which still have the property that they're stable under multiplication by R, but they're still not everything, they're still a lattice. Those are called fractional ideals.
column2: 举个例子，若 R 是高斯整数环——这里是高斯整数环 R，我们可能会有分式理想 I，也就是——抱歉，这是 Z[i]——我们可能有理想 (1/2)R，它就是这里的这些格点，它是一个点阵，只是没有包含在 R 中，明白吗？所以你可以得到比 R 稍大的对象，仍然保持在 R 的乘法下稳定的性质，但它们仍然不是整个域，依然是格点。这些就称为分式理想。

column1: And just as we had multiplication of ideals, it generalizes to multiplication of fractional ideals—and we're going to see right away why we wanted to go to fractional ideals—namely, if I have two fractional ideals, I define the product I * J as the collection of all sums sum alpha_i beta_i, i = 1 to n, such that alpha_i is in the fractional ideal I and beta_i is in the fractional ideal J.
column2: 正如我们之前定义了理想的乘法，它可以推广到分式理想的乘法——我们马上就会明白为什么要引入分式理想——即如果我有两个分式理想，我定义乘积 I * J 为所有有限和 sum alpha_i beta_i (i=1 到 n) 的集合，使得 alpha_i 属于分式理想 I，beta_i 属于分式理想 J。

column1: So it's the natural fractional ideal you'd get by taking all the products which you'd have to have, and then taking all sums of those things because it's got to be stable under addition, and then that's closed under multiplication by R.
column2: 因此这是取所有乘积后所得到的自然分式理想，你必须包含这些乘积，并取其全部有限和，因为加法必须封闭，而且它在 R 的乘法下也是封闭的。

column1: So this is a very complicated idea of multiplying ideals, and you probably did this for your homework and you did it on Friday. It's not a priori clear when you multiply two ideals, what ideal you get.
column2: 因此这是理想乘法的一个非常复杂的概念，你们作业里可能做过，周五也做过。事先并不显然：当你把两个理想相乘时会得到什么理想。

column1: However, there is one really simple case: by the way, if you multiply two principal ideals, if you multiply (alpha * R) * (beta * R), that's the only case where it's simple, and the answer is you get the principal ideal generated by alpha * beta.
column2: 然而，有一种非常简单的情况：如果你乘两个主理想，如果你乘(alpha * R) * (beta * R)，那是唯一简单的情形，结果就是由 alpha * beta 生成的主理想。

column1: It's the only simple case, and the reason is that everything in here is of the form alpha * r, and everything in here is of the form beta * r' , and if you multiply something here times something here, it's of the form alpha * beta * r * r', and taking sums doesn't change that. So you've got another fractional ideal of this form.
column2: 这是唯一简单的情况，原因是这里面的所有元素都形如 alpha * r，而那里的所有元素都形如 beta * r'，当你把此处的元素与彼处的元素相乘，它形如 alpha * beta * r * r'，求和并不会改变形式。所以你得到了这种形式的另一个分式理想。

column1: So multiplying this ideal by a principal ideal—so if I wanted to multiply this by the ideal J, say generated by 2 + i, that's an ideal of norm 5, if I multiplied I * J, I get the ideal generated by (1 + i)/2 * R. So principal ideals are easy to multiply, but general ideals or general fractional ideals are very mysterious.
column2: 因此把这个理想乘以一个主理想——比如我想把它乘以理想 J，设 J 是由 2 + i 生成的理想，其范数为 5；若我将 I * J 相乘，便得到由 (1 + i)/2 生成的理想 ((1 + i)/2)R。所以主理想很容易相乘，但一般理想或一般分式理想则非常神秘。

column1: Okay, now the big result which Peter probably talked in a slightly different way about last time is the following proposition, and this was proved at the end of the 19th century by a number of mathematicians, Kummer, Dedekind: that the fractional ideals form a group under multiplication. That's the first statement, (1).
column2: 好，现在彼得上次可能以略微不同的方式讲过的一个重要命题如下，它是在 19 世纪末由多位数学家证明的：库默尔与戴德金证明了：分式理想在乘法下构成一个群。这是第一条陈述 (1)。

column1: So what is the content of that? Well, it's pretty clear that this is a commutative operation: I * J is the same as J * I. It's also clear, since multiplication is associative, it's an associative operation.
column2: 那么它的内涵是什么呢？首先很显然这是交换运算：I * J 与 J * I相同；同样显然的是，乘法满足结合律，它是结合运算。

column1: So what you have to be able to do to prove a result like that is to figure out what's the identity object and what's the inverse object. Now the identity object is pretty clear: can someone tell me which fractional ideal under this crazy kind of multiplication will take a fractional ideal into itself? R, good! The identity is the ideal R, yeah, which is generated by 1. So that's pretty clear that I * R is equal to R * I, which is equal to I.
column2: 因此要证明这样的结论，你所要做的就是搞清楚什么是单位元对象，什么是逆元对象。单位元对象相当明确：谁能告诉我，在这种奇妙的乘法下，哪个分式理想乘以任意分式理想仍得其自身？R，很好！单位元就是理想 R，对，它由 1 生成。如果你把任何理想乘以 R，看一下定义，你只是把该理想中的元素乘以 R 中的元素再求和，它们依然是该理想中的元素。所以显然 I * R = R * I = I。

column1: That's easy; what's hard is to prove that there's an inverse ideal. That's the content of this theorem: existence of an inverse such that I times a new ideal, maybe I^{-1}, is the ideal R. That's not clear at all.
column2: 这很容易；难点在于证明逆理想的存在性。这正是本定理的核心所在：存在逆元，使得 I 乘以一个新理想 I^{-1}等于理想 R。这绝非显然。

column1: It is clear for principal ideals: what would be an inverse to the principal ideal alpha * R? Exactly, alpha is a nonzero number, so in the field you can write 1/alpha, right? And 1/alpha still gives a fractional ideal, which is why we needed fractional ideals to be able to invert things.
column2: 但对主理想来说是显然的：主理想 alpha * R 的逆是什么？没错，alpha 是非零数，所以在域中你可以写出 1/alpha，对吧？而 1/alpha 仍给出一个分式理想，这就是为什么我们需要分式理想来实现求逆。

On the other hand, if you multiply the principal ideal alpha * R, the only possibility for its inverse is (1/alpha)R, which is R, and that's why we have to introduce fractional ideals to even invert principal ideals. We'd have to introduce these.
column2: 如果 alpha 属于 R \ {0}，1/alpha 就在域 Q(√D) 中，但可能不在 R 中。另一方面，如果你乘主理想 alpha * R，其逆的唯一可能就是 (1/alpha)R，乘积为 R，这就是为什么哪怕仅仅为了对主理想求逆，我们也必须引入分式理想。

column1: The second proposition is: the principal ideals form a subgroup. Well, that's clear, right? If you multiply two principal ideals, you get another principal ideal; the identity is a principal ideal generated by 1; and the inverse of a principal ideal is a principal fractional ideal.
column2: 第二个命题是：主理想构成一个子群。这显然成立，对吧？两主理想相乘仍是主理想；单位元是由 1 生成的主理想；而主理想的逆也是主分式理想。

column1: Okay, so you have the fractional ideals form a group under multiplication, the principal ideals form a subgroup. Now if every ideal were principal, then this subgroup would be the entire group. If every ideal is not principal, then there are some things in the group that aren't in the subgroup. So it suggests that we should look at the quotient group, right? That would measure how far we are away from being a principal ideal domain; it's a concrete measure.
column2: 因此分式理想在乘法下成群，主理想构成其子群。现在如果每个理想都是主理想，那么这个子群就是全群。如果并非每个理想都是主理想，群里就会有一些元素不在子群中。这启示我们应该考察商群，对吧？它能衡量我们距离主理想整环有多远；这是一个具体的度量。

column1: All right, and that's the third section: the quotient group, which I'll call C_D, because it depends on this discriminant D, is a finite group, which is called the ideal class group.
column2: 好的，这就是第三个命题：商群我记为 C_D（因为它依赖于判别式 D），是一个有限群，称为理想类群。

column1: So Peter defined that last time, without going to fractional ideals, by putting an equivalence relation on the set of all ideals. But it's a little classier, at least from our point of view, because we know about groups and subgroups and quotient groups, to first define an abelian group—this is of course an abelian group.
column2: 彼得上节课在没有引入分式理想的情况下，通过在所有理想的集合上建立等价关系定义了它。但从我们的角度来看，先定义一个阿贝尔群要显得更优雅一些，因为我们熟知群、子群和商群。这当然是一个阿贝尔群。

column1: Now this group is infinite: if you take any prime ideal and just take its powers, so that you get arbitrarily, you get an infinite number of ideals. So this is an infinite abelian group; this subgroup is also infinite. But the miracle is: when you go to the quotient group, it's finite! So things are close to being a principal ideal domain.
column2: 注意这个群是无限群：若取任一素理想并取其幂次，你就会得到无穷多个理想。所以这是无限阿贝尔群，主理想子群也是无限的。但奇迹在于：当你取商群时，它居然是有限的！所以情况非常接近主理想整环。

column1: There are rings, by the way, where you have this is true, you have this is true, and then the quotient group is infinite. So this is a nice statement about these rings: that the quotient group is finite.
column2: 顺便提一句，有些环满足第一、二条，但商群却是无限的。因此对我们这些环来说，商群有限是一个极好的性质。

column1: And once you have this theorem—and people were very excited to find this theorem—you have a measure of how far away you are from being a principal ideal domain, and that measure is, in some sense, the order of this quotient group, the class group, and they gave that a name: so we let h_D be the order of the ideal class group C_D.
column2: 一旦你有了这个定理——人们发现此定理时极其兴奋——你就有了衡量偏离主理想整环程度的指标，而该度量在某种意义上就是该商群（类群）的阶，人们给它起了一个名字：我们令 h_D为理想类群 C_D 的阶。

column1: And once Dedekind and Kummer had identified this group and identified its order as a very important invariant of this ring, it became an interesting question to compute it, right? And to tabulate it, because if we could find examples where the class group was non-trivial, those are examples of non-principal ideal domains.
column2: 一旦戴德金与库默尔确定了这个群及其阶作为环的一个极其重要的不变量，计算它并列出表格就成了一个非常有趣的问题，对吧？因为如果我们能找到类群非平凡的例子，那就是非主理想整环的例证。

column1: So here's a table; I'll give you the first couple of discriminants: -3, -4, -7, -8, -11, -15, -19, -20, -23. So we've tabulated these discriminants before, and then I'll put next to them: what is the class number? So here the class number is 1, here the class number is 1, here the class number is 1, here's the class number is 1. This looks very bad: the class number is always 1, it's always a principal ideal domain! But when you get to -15, the class number is 2; -19, it's 1; -20, it's 2; -23, the class number is 3.
column2: 这里有一张表，我给出前几个判别式：-3、-4、-7、-8、-11、-15、-19、-20、-23。我们之前列出过这些判别式，接着我在旁边写出它们的类数是多少？这里类数是 1，这里是 1，这里是 1，这里也是 1。这看起来情况不妙：类数总是 1，全都是主理想整环！但当你走到 -15 时，类数是 2；-19 时是 1；-20 时是 2；-23 时类数是 3。

column1: And people made—Gauss, because he was thinking in slightly different terms, but Gauss and Dirichlet made elaborate tables of these class numbers, and they found that the class numbers appeared to be growing.
column2: 人们——高斯（虽然他是以略微不同的术语思考的），高斯与狄利克雷制作了详尽的类数表，他们发现类数似乎在持续增长。

column1: And in fact, the last time h_D is equal to 1 is D = -163. They didn't find any other principal ideal domains; there were only finitely many of the rings on this list that were principal ideal domains.
column2: 事实上，h_D = 1 最后一次出现是在 D = -163。他们没有找到任何其他的主理想整环；在这份列表中只有有限多个环是主理想整环。

column1: And in fact, it appeared that h_D was growing as the absolute value of D was growing, and Gauss guessed that the size of h_D was approximately the square root of |D|.
column2: 事实上，随着|D| 的绝对值增大，h_D 似乎也在增长，高斯猜测 h_D 的大小约为 √|D|。

column1: So as a function of the discriminant, these rings were getting more and more and more complicated: if you had a discriminant which was 10 to the 100th power, had a hundred digits in it, you would expect the class number that had 50 digits in it—still a finite number, but large.
column2: 因此作为判别式的函数，这些环变得越来越复杂：如果判别式达到 10^100，有 100 位数字，你就会预期类数有 50 位数字——虽然仍是有限数，但极其庞大。

column1: And Gauss had a lot of experimental evidence for this, but couldn't prove it, and it became known as Gauss's class number problem.
column2: 高斯为此拥有大量的数值计算证据，但无法证明它，这后来被称为高斯类数问题。

column1: Okay, now in fact the correct estimates—this is kind of vague because it doesn't tell you—I mean, more precisely, what Gauss conjectured is that the class number with respect to D is less than some constant times |D| to the one-half times the log of the absolute value of D, and is greater than some other constant C' times |D| to the one-half divided by the log of the absolute value of D. column2: 好，现在我们来看看高斯整数环对应的情形，因为在那里我们已经彻底算清了一切，可以明确看到得到的是什么级数。对于高斯整数 Z[i]，可以算出该 L(s)长成这样：对 p ≡ 1 mod 4（那些有两个因子的素数）的乘积 prod (1 - 1/p^s)^{-1}，以及对 p ≡ 3 mod 4 的乘积 prod (1 + 1/p^s)^{-1}。而在p = 2 处则什么都不剩，因为那里的项完全抵消了。

column1: And notice that even though this thing doesn't converge at s equal 1, and likewise this thing doesn't converge at s equal 1, because you can you can prove that the quotient does converge at s equal 1. column1: But once you take this product, you get, you know, sum over—it turns out—n prime to the discriminant and bigger than equal to 1, plus or minus over 1 over n to the s, and there's enough cancellation so that Dirichlet proved that L of 1 exists, and he found a formula for it called the class number formula, which was his great achievement! And Dirichlet's class number formula is a formula for L of 1 in terms of the ring: that it's equal to 2 pi over the square root of the absolute value of the discriminant, times the class number of the ring, divided by the number of units.
column2: 但一旦取商之后，结果是对与判别式互素的 n >= 1 求和，带有正负号 (± 1)/n^s，其中的正负抵消足以让狄利克雷证明 L(1)存在，并且他找到了一个关于它的公式，称为类数公式，这是他的伟大成就！狄利克雷类数公式将 L(1)用环的不变量表示：它等于 2π/√|D| 乘以环的类数，除以单位元个数 w！

column1: Is that a great formula or what? column2: 这个公式是不是极其宏伟？我们来看看它在这里说了什么：它说明无论这个级数和是多少，它都等于 2π/√|D|——也就是 √4，因为判别式是 -4——乘以高斯整数环的类数（假设我们事先未知），除以单位元个数 4！没错，高斯整数有 4 个单位元，因此得到 (π/4) * h。根据狄利克雷公式，无论它收敛到什么，必定收敛到 π/4 的某个整数倍。

column1: So you could never give, for example, a list of the things where the class number was 1, because they could have always been one more. So it was rather unsatisfactory result. column1: So Goldfeld had this wonderful idea, and he said: look, Siegel's zero doesn't really exist anyhow, but I do know how to make other functions like this, with products and everything.
